title: Canonical restriction from a higher-direct-image stalk to strict-local cohomology
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and $g:S_{(\bar s)}\to S$ the structural morphism [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map] of the strict henselization, the limit of the pointed affine etale neighbourhoods [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. For an abelian etale sheaf $G$ on $S$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], the restriction $r_G:G_{\bar s}\to\Gamma(S_{(\bar s)},g^{-1}G)$ is the map induced from the restrictions over pointed etale neighbourhoods [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor]: for an affine pointed etale neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$ of the chosen representative category, apply the inverse-image unit on sections over $V$ and restrict along the section $S_{(\bar s)}\to V\times_S S_{(\bar s)}$ given by the limit leg $S_{(\bar s)}\to V$. These maps are compatible with pointed morphisms, and the affine pointed neighbourhoods are cofinal [lemma-weil-pbc-affine-neighbourhood-cofinal], so there is exactly one map $r_G$ out of the stalk colimit whose composite with the germ map of every such $(V,\bar v)$ is the given restriction; $r_G$ is defined as this map. Global sections on $S_{(\bar s)}$ are exact, as on every strictly henselian local scheme.

For any morphism $f:X\to S$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], any abelian etale sheaf $F$ on $X$, and $q\in\mathbf N$, put $X'=X\times_S S_{(\bar s)}$, with projections $p:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S_{(\bar s)}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Define the canonical restriction
$$\rho^q_{f,F,\bar s}:(R^qf_*F)_{\bar s}\longrightarrow H^q(X'_{\mathrm{Et}},p^{-1}F)$$
[def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] as follows: apply $r$ to $R^qf_*F$; commute exact derived inverse image [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] with cohomology; apply the degree-$q$ cohomology of the derived base-change mate $g^{-1}Rf_*F\to Rf'_*p^{-1}F$ (the mate of the canonical pullback-composition isomorphism under the derived adjunctions of inverse and direct image [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction]); then identify $\Gamma(S_{(\bar s)},\mathcal H^q(Rf'_*p^{-1}F))$ with $H^q(X'_{\mathrm{Et}},p^{-1}F)$ using exactness of global sections and the canonical Leray composition isomorphism. This defines a specific map, with no isomorphism assertion for $\rho$ built into its definition.

proof.text: For the germ restriction, use the initial representative affine pointed-neighbourhood functor of strictHenselizationAffineProperties (def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit). Its opposite is final. Mathlib GrothendieckTopology.Point.isColimitPresheafFiberCocone and Functor.Final.isColimitWhiskerEquiv identify the stalk germ cocone restricted to these representatives as a colimit.

For a pointed transition t: V_j → V_i, compare the two projections of the pullback to prove section_j ≫ g.Etale.map t = section_i. The second projection is the identity; the first is the limit-cone naturality equation followed by the natural affine-spectrum identification (Mathlib Scheme.isoSpec_inv_naturality and Scheme.isoSpec_Spec_inv). Naturality of the inverse-image adjunction unit then gives F.map t.op ≫ restriction_j = restriction_i. These are the cocone equations. Descend this cocone using IsColimit.desc; IsColimit.fac gives the required germ equations, and IsColimit.hom_ext gives uniqueness.

For exact global sections, give Ω its canonical algebra structure over the residue field of the geometric image. Clause (1) of lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality, namely strictHenselizationResidue, supplies the strictly henselian local ring structure on strictHenselization s. The already proved source-library declaration Scheme.preservesEpimorphisms_sheafSections_of_isStrictlyHenselianLocalRing (WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.StrictlyHenselian, Stacks 03QO) supplies preservation of epimorphisms by evaluation at the terminal etale object. Transport it to global sections through Sheaf.ΓNatIsoSheafSections. Global sections preserve kernels and are additive; Mathlib Functor.preservesHomology_of_preservesEpis_and_kernels and Functor.preservesFiniteColimits_of_preservesHomology give the stated exactness.
